answer: Each agent must lock a stake in a shared vault before it can transact, so every fake identity costs real money. A reputation graph then treats each agent as a vertex: new vertices start with no trust edges, and trust only accrues through verified, paid work. Like a pigment that cannot be faked without the dye, reputation cannot be copied — an attacker spinning up thousands of vertices still holds zero trust and zero stake-weighted influence, so the Sybil flood costs more than it earns.
